text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Tuesday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- President Guntis Ulmanis leaves for a three-day visit to Denmark, accompanied by a delegation of Latvian entrepreneurs.
- Representatives of Latvia and Finland have signed a visa-free agreement between the countries.
- The newly elected Riga city council is due to hold its first meeting on March 25.
- Fatherland & Freedom and LNNK have agreed to form a joint 13-deputy faction in the Riga city council to outweigh the Social democrats.

- The Latvian railway company estimates the damages of the railway crash between Riga and Ventspils to run at several hundred thousand lats. The company announced that it would sue for damages the owner of the truck which caused the crash.
- The second GSM mobile phone operator, Baltcom GSM, has begun business operations in Latvia. American Western Wireless and Metromedia have a 49 percent stake in the firm.

- President Ulmanis once again speaks critically of Latvia's parties and says the nation needs a party with at least 30 percent support from voters. In an interview with the Baltic News Service Ulmanis announced that he wants to see the ruling coalition more consolidated.
- The search for Swedish professor Jan Akke Delenbrandt continues without any results. Police have searched the port area in Liepaja and now intend use divers to search the city's water reservoirs.

- The project for construction of the Latvian trade centre in Moscow was presented to Latvia's foreign Ministry. The centre with a cost around $1.3 million will include a set of facilities necessary for Latvian entrepreneurs to promote their exports in Russia, such as a customs warehouse, cold storage facilities, transport, exhibition hall and marketing service. The entrepreneurs, in turn, believe the cost of the project to be underestimated and say they prefer doing their business without mediators.
- Neste and Statoil have signed an agreement with the Riga port authority on building an oil terminal in Riga.
